stops.title: 1. Load the stops
stops.body: Pick a scenario, import a CSV or generate random stops. They show up as dots on the map.

fleet.title: 2. Review the fleet and constraints
fleet.body: This is where you define couriers, vehicles, capacity, shifts and time windows.

algorithm.title: 3. Choose algorithm and objective
algorithm.body: Each one explores differently. Hover the ⓘ icons to understand every parameter.

optimize.title: 4. Optimize and watch it work
optimize.body: Routes draw themselves, ants explore and metrics improve live. You can stop whenever you want.

landing.title: Optimize delivery routes with genetic algorithms and ant colonies
landing.subtitle: Plan last-mile delivery in Monterrey with memetic GA, ACO, the ACO+GA hybrid and NSGA-II on real streets. Watch them work: routes draw themselves, ants explore and metrics improve live.

split.title: Split: from tour to routes
split.body: The chromosome is a permutation of stops. Split walks the tour and cuts it into consecutive segments, one per driver, respecting capacity and shift.
split.note: Cuts and vehicle order of the 40-stop demo solution.
split.aria: Stop tour cut into one segment per driver

pheromone.title: Pheromone: reinforcing the best route
pheromone.body: In MMAS only the best ant deposits pheromone. The edges of its route are reinforced and the rest evaporate every iteration, with minimum and maximum bounds to avoid stagnation.
pheromone.note: First 9 stops of demo route 1. Faint edges: 3 nearest neighbors.
pheromone.aria: Stop graph with the edges of the best route reinforced

pareto.title: Pareto front: time versus cost
pareto.body: NSGA-II does not pick a single winner. It returns the solutions that cannot improve one objective without worsening another, and you choose the trade-off.
pareto.note: Conceptual sketch, not to scale. Point size encodes the number of drivers.
pareto.aria: Scatter of solutions with the non-dominated front joined by a step line

distance.title: Distance
distance.body: Kilometers driven by all couriers combined, on real streets. Less distance usually means less fuel and wear.

cost.title: Cost
cost.body: Fuel, hourly wages and fixed vehicle costs, in pesos. If it grows too much, try fewer couriers or shorter routes.

duration.title: Total time
duration.body: Sum of every route's duration: driving, service at each stop and waiting. It measures labor spent, not when the day ends.

makespan.title: Last delivery
makespan.body: When the longest route finishes. Lowering it means the last customer is served sooner, which requires spreading load more evenly.

vehicles.title: Couriers
vehicles.body: How many couriers go out. Fewer couriers save fixed costs, but routes get longer and closer to the shift limit.

lateness.title: Lateness
lateness.body: Accumulated minutes of arrivals outside the time window, weighted by priority. Zero is ideal; being late to an urgent stop weighs three times more.

gap.title: Gap
gap.body: How far a run is from the best one, as a fitness percentage. 0% is the best; 5% means 5% worse than the winner.

fitness.title: Fitness
fitness.body: A single number combining time, cost, vehicles and penalties according to your weights. Lower is better; use it to compare solutions of the same problem.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.body: Real seconds the algorithm took to deliver this solution.

feasible.title: Feasible
feasible.body: The solution respects capacity and shift limits and delivers every stop. Time window lateness is soft and does not make it infeasible.

time_limit_s.title: Time limit
time_limit_s.body: Maximum seconds the algorithm may think. More time usually gives better routes with diminishing returns; less time answers fast but rougher.
time_limit_s.example: 10 s for a demo, 60 s for 200 stops

max_iterations.title: Max iterations
max_iterations.body: Cap on generations or cycles. It stops at this cap or at the time limit, whichever comes first.

seed.title: Seed
seed.body: Makes randomness reproducible: the same seed gives the same result. Change it to explore a different solution.

init.title: Initialization
init.body: How the starting population or solution is built. K-means groups by zone, nearest neighbor is greedy, sweep rotates around the depot and random uses no heuristic.

local_search.title: Local search
local_search.body: Polishes each solution by moving or swapping stops while cost improves. On gives better routes for a bit more compute.

progress_every.title: Report every
progress_every.body: How many iterations between progress updates on screen. A low number makes the chart smoother with more traffic.

progress_interval_s.title: Progress interval
progress_interval_s.body: Minimum seconds between progress updates sent to the screen.

pop_size.title: Population
pop_size.body: How many solutions compete in each generation. A bigger population explores better but each generation takes longer.

crossover_rate.title: Crossover rate
crossover_rate.body: How often two parents combine their routes into a child. High mixes a lot; low keeps what already works.

mutation_rate.title: Mutation rate
mutation_rate.body: How often a child is randomly altered. Raising it avoids getting stuck; lowering it fine-tunes what exists.

ls_rate.title: Local search rate
ls_rate.body: Fraction of children polished with local search. Higher gives better children but is slower.

elite_size.title: Elite
elite_size.body: How many of the best solutions pass untouched to the next generation, so progress is not lost.

tournament_size.title: Tournament size
tournament_size.body: How many contenders are drawn when picking a parent. Bigger puts more pressure toward the best.

crossover.title: Crossover operator
crossover.body: OX keeps the relative order of stops from a parent; PMX keeps positions. Both produce a valid tour.

stagnation_generations.title: Generations without improvement
stagnation_generations.body: If nothing improves for this many generations, the algorithm stops or partially restarts.

granular_k.title: Granular neighbors
granular_k.body: For each stop only its k nearest neighbors are tried. Lower is faster; higher checks more moves.

n_ants.title: Ants
n_ants.body: How many ants build a solution each iteration. More ants explore more and take longer.

alpha.title: Alpha (pheromone)
alpha.body: How much pheromone weighs when choosing the next stop. High follows the trail; low ignores experience.

beta.title: Beta (heuristic)
beta.body: How much closeness weighs when choosing the next stop. High is greedy toward the nearest; low follows pheromone more.

rho.title: Evaporation (ρ)
rho.body: Fraction of pheromone that evaporates each iteration. High forgets fast and explores; low reinforces and converges sooner.

q0.title: q0 (exploitation)
q0.body: Probability of picking the best option directly instead of sampling. High is greedier; low explores more.

cand_k.title: Candidates per node
cand_k.body: How many nearby stops an ant considers as the next step. Fewer candidates speed up construction.

tw_weight.title: Time window weight
tw_weight.body: How much time windows influence the next-stop choice. Higher prioritizes arriving on time.

ls_ants.title: Ants with local search
ls_ants.body: How many of each iteration's best ants are polished with local search.

stagnation_iterations.title: Iterations without improvement
stagnation_iterations.body: If nothing improves for this many iterations, pheromone is reset to explore again.

ls_every.title: Local search every
ls_every.body: Every how many generations local search is applied. 0 turns it off and speeds up NSGA-II.

ga_generations_per_cycle.title: Generations per cycle
ga_generations_per_cycle.body: How many GA generations run before handing over to the ants.

ants_per_cycle.title: Ants per cycle
ants_per_cycle.body: How many ants build solutions in each cycle of the hybrid.

elite_deposit.title: Depositing elite
elite_deposit.body: How many GA solutions reinforce the ants' pheromone.

inject_k.title: Injected solutions
inject_k.body: How many ant solutions enter the GA population each cycle.

seed_ants.title: Seeding ants
seed_ants.body: Ants used to seed the initial population. Empty lets the algorithm decide.

adaptive.title: Adaptive
adaptive.body: Gives more time to the method (GA or ACO) that is improving most.

ga_crossover.title: GA crossover
ga_crossover.body: OX keeps the relative order of stops; PMX keeps positions.

ga_crossover_rate.title: GA crossover rate
ga_crossover_rate.body: How often two GA parents combine their routes.

ga_mutation_rate.title: GA mutation rate
ga_mutation_rate.body: How often a GA child is randomly altered.

ga_ls_rate.title: GA local search rate
ga_ls_rate.body: Fraction of GA children polished with local search.

ga_elite_size.title: GA elite
ga_elite_size.body: How many best GA solutions pass untouched to the next generation.

ga_stagnation_generations.title: GA stagnation
ga_stagnation_generations.body: Generations without improvement after which the GA yields to the ants.

aco_alpha.title: ACO alpha
aco_alpha.body: How much pheromone weighs when choosing the next stop.

aco_beta.title: ACO beta
aco_beta.body: How much closeness weighs when choosing the next stop.

aco_rho.title: ACO evaporation
aco_rho.body: Fraction of pheromone that evaporates each cycle.

aco_cand_k.title: ACO candidates
aco_cand_k.body: How many nearby stops an ant considers as the next step.

aco_stagnation_cycles.title: ACO stagnation
aco_stagnation_cycles.body: Cycles without improvement after which pheromone is reset.

objectives.title: Objectives
objectives.body: Which objectives NSGA-II compares to build the Pareto front.

title.title: Objective
title.body: What the algorithm cares about most when comparing solutions. Changing it changes the weights of time, cost, vehicles and last delivery.

fastest.title: Fastest
fastest.body: Prioritizes the last route finishing as early as possible. Spreads load evenly, even if it costs more.

cheapest.title: Cheapest
cheapest.body: Prioritizes total cost. Tends to bundle stops into fewer, longer routes.

fewest.title: Fewest couriers
fewest.body: Prioritizes using few vehicles. Each extra courier is a fixed cost.

balanced.title: Balanced
balanced.body: Splits the weight between time, cost and vehicles. A good starting point.

weights.title: Objective weights
weights.body: How much each objective is worth against the others. They are normalized to sum to 1: only the proportion matters.

time.title: Total time weight
time.body: Raising it reduces the sum of hours across all couriers.

cost.title: Cost weight
cost.body: Raising it favors routes cheaper in fuel, wages and fixed costs.

vehicles.title: Vehicles weight
vehicles.body: Raising it pushes toward using fewer couriers.

makespan.title: Last delivery weight
makespan.body: Raising it balances routes so they all finish around the same time.

capacity_kg.title: Weight capacity
capacity_kg.body: Each route cannot carry more kg than its vehicle. Turning it off allows shorter but unrealistic routes.

capacity_m3.title: Volume capacity
capacity_m3.body: Each route cannot carry more m³ than its vehicle. It matters with large, light parcels.

time_windows.title: Time windows
time_windows.body: Each customer asks for a range of hours. Arriving early forces waiting and arriving late is penalized.

max_shift.title: Max shift
max_shift.body: A route cannot last longer than the courier's shift. Turning it off allows fewer couriers but long shifts.

priorities.title: Priorities
priorities.body: High priority stops weigh 3 times more when measuring lateness; low ones, half.

title.title: Algorithm
title.body: The method that searches for routes. All receive the same problem; they differ in how they explore and how much time they need.

ga.title: Memetic GA
ga.body: Evolves a population of routes through crossover and mutation, and polishes each child with local search. A solid all-rounder.

aco.title: ACO (MMAS)
aco.body: Virtual ants build routes following a pheromone trail that is reinforced on the best ones. Shines on routes with clear structure.

aco_ga.title: ACO + GA
aco_ga.body: Hybrid: the GA and the ants hand each other their best solutions. Often wins on big problems, with more parameters.

nsga2.title: NSGA-II
nsga2.body: Multi-objective: it returns not one route set but a Pareto front of trade-offs between time, cost and vehicles.

pyvrp.title: PyVRP
pyvrp.body: State-of-the-art reference solver. Useful to measure how far the others are.

ortools.title: OR-Tools
ortools.body: Google's routing solver, fast and robust. Useful as a comparison point.

depot.title: Single depot
depot.body: All couriers leave the same depot and return to it. The classic distribution center case.

multi_origin.title: Multi-origin
multi_origin.body: Each courier starts from their own point, such as home. With no end point, the route is open and ends at the last delivery.

fitness.title: Best fitness
fitness.body: A single number summarizing how good the best solution found is. Lower is better; the curve drops as the algorithm learns.

time.title: Time
time.body: Real seconds elapsed since the run started.

logScale.title: Log scale
logScale.body: Each tick is ten times the previous one. Useful when curves start very high and then flatten.

size.title: Point size
size.body: How many vehicles each solution uses: bigger point, more couriers.

pareto.title: Front axes
pareto.body: Each point is a solution. Choose which two objectives to compare; front points are those no other solution beats on both.

trigger.title: When to re-optimize
trigger.body: Per order: each new order triggers a recompute. Per batch: orders accumulate and a recompute runs every so often.

speed.title: Speed
speed.body: Simulated minutes per real second. At 60x a simulated hour passes in a second.

split.title: Split
split.body: Algorithm that cuts a long tour of stops into one route per courier, respecting capacity and shift and picking the cheapest cuts.

pheromone.title: Pheromone
pheromone.body: Virtual trail ants leave on the edges of good routes. It evaporates over time and guides the next ants.

pareto.title: Pareto front
pareto.body: Set of solutions where improving one objective forces worsening another. You pick the trade-off.

makespan.title: Makespan
makespan.body: The moment the last route of the day finishes. Reducing it balances load between couriers.

timeWindow.title: Time window
timeWindow.body: Range of hours when the customer can receive. Arriving early forces waiting; arriving late is penalized.

localSearch.title: Local search
localSearch.body: Polishing a solution with small changes, like moving a stop or reversing a segment, while they improve cost.

kmeans.title: K-means
kmeans.body: Groups stops by proximity into k zones. Used to start with compact routes per courier.

gap.title: Gap
gap.body: Percentage difference against the best known solution. 0% means matching it.
